question: Does matched post-training allocation to state transitions preserve or improve self-composition while endpoint-only allocation erases it?

initial.treatment: A fresh two-epoch 50/50 encoder-transition adapter, evaluated without continuation.

transition.treatment: One matched epoch with transition producers and the same consumer targets.

endpoint.treatment: One matched epoch with encoder producers and the same consumer targets.

mixed.treatment: One matched epoch with the same 50/50 producer mixture and consumer targets.

matched_contract: All continuation arms fork the exact initial adapter.
All continuation arms use the same semantic programs and held-out test bank.
All continuation arms use 20,000 forwards, 20,000 one-token targets, and 5,120,000 fixed-padding tokens.
All continuation arms share optimizer, learning rate, batch order seed, and update count.
Only the producer target allocation differs; consumer targets remain fixed.

prepared_data.validation: All four real program banks passed the existing tokenizer, code-alphabet, length, split, and compute checks.

initial_gate_repair.diagnosis: The fresh initial arm used only two-step training cases, unlike the proven initial curriculum, and failed producer competence while retaining a perfect consumer.
initial_gate_repair.repair: Restore one- and two-step training and validation examples only in the initial arm. Continuation arms remain two-step-only, as in the prior pipeline.
initial_gate_repair.unchanged: The test bank, continuation data and compute, treatments, thresholds, causal diagnostics, and analysis unit remain locked. No continuation outcome existed when this repair was made.
initial_gate_repair.independent_review: Claude Opus 5: GO; changing all arms would dilute the two-step transition treatment, so scope the repair to the initial arm.

estimands: At h16, transition minus mixed replay answer accuracy.
At h16, endpoint minus mixed replay answer accuracy.
primary_screen.analysis_unit: Held-out program context; rows pair across exact test IDs.
primary_screen.short_horizon_parity: At h2, absolute transition-minus-mixed and endpoint-minus-mixed gaps must each be at most 0.05.
primary_screen.go: The hard-cut code chain is causally used, short-horizon parity passes, transition exceeds mixed at h16, and endpoint falls below mixed at h16.
primary_screen.stop: Any consumer or h2 competence failure, no causal code following, or no h16 allocation effect.

required_diagnostics: Absolute accuracy for all four arms at every horizon.
Gold-code consumer accuracy and conditional semantic transition accuracy.
A valid mid-chain code intervention whose final answer follows the forced semantic state.
Exact surface-code accuracy beside semantic-state and final-answer accuracy.
Final train and validation loss for all continuation arms.

claim_boundary.in_scope: Allocation of matched post-training targets changes whether a learned finite update interface composes over unseen longer histories.
claim_boundary.out_of_scope: Novel transition supervision, unseen state-operation pairs, natural-language reasoning in general, or a universal law of reusable states.

literature_boundary: Supervised Memory Training already trains one-step memory dynamics in recurrent networks (Kumar and Isola, 2026).
Markovian Transformers already makes an intermediate text state causally necessary for answer prediction.
The target result is a controlled post-training preservation-and-erasure effect, not a new training method.
independent_review: Claude Opus 5: GO for a fresh Qwen screening seed after adding mixed replay, short-horizon parity, a hard context cut, and a mid-chain valid-code intervention; unseen transition-pair generalization is a separate claim.
